wiki.Venue market:
# Bay Area wedding venue comparison
Status: Research ongoing. Current counts and unresolved leads are in the dated discovery review; no exhaustive coverage claimed.

## Coverage
Current census scope: the nine Bay Area counties. Adjacent-county leads are excluded from census counts; borderline parcels are held pending verification. Deduplicate by operator/property while keeping distinct spaces/packages. Track official URL, discovery source, active/closed/unconfirmed status, checked dates and gaps. No exhaustive inventory claimed.

## Comparison fields
- Capacity: seated dinner plus dance floor vs standing; indoor and weather-backup capacity.
- Prices: venue-only vs package, headcount/day/season/duration/year, minimum spend, ceremony fee, extra hours, all mandatory taxes/service/rental/staff/security/cleanup charges, deposits/refunds/cancellation.
- Inclusions: venue, chairs/tables, basic rentals, decor, setup/reset, kitchen/prep space, getting-ready rooms, exclusivity.
- Outside vendors: approved lists, fees/restrictions, catering and alcohol/BYOB/bartender rules.
- Hours: separate indoor/outdoor amplified music, alcohol service, guest departure and cleanup. Midnight status needs evidence.
- Travel: parking/shuttle, nearby hotels, airports/cities, date/time-dependent road journeys; lodging room/capacity/exclusivity.
- Other: restrooms, accessibility, rain/heat/smoke backup, power/lighting/storage/load-in, decoration/fire rules, insurance, permitted annual events and public availability.

## Normalization and economics
Compare full mandatory customer cost at stated headcount/date/duration; show food/drink inclusions. Refundable deposits are cash requirements, not automatically expenses. Label quote-only, starting-at, verified published values and modeled values separately.

Price does not reveal profit. Low/base/high scenarios need realized booking revenue, bookings/seasonality, per-event labor/cleanup/security/rentals, fixed rent/utilities/insurance/marketing/maintenance, owner pay, startup capital and booking-ramp cash reserves.

## Planned charts
Comparable mandatory price vs capacity; hours/vendor flexibility; geography/travel; break-even bookings/seasonality. No numerical charts until enough comparable sourced observations exist.
## Research scope clarification — 2026-10-11T03:38:07Z
- Calculate realistic capital requirements from the evidence; do not impose an upfront budget ceiling or repeat the budget-cap question.
- Compare four routes without selecting one: lease an existing lawful venue; convert leased space; buy land and develop; buy an established venue.
- Desired ability to host 300–400 guests. Whether this is normal or peak capacity remains unknown; no minimum/approved occupancy established.
- Prefer open/separated space to reduce noise issues, but acreage does not establish permitted event use, midnight hours or sound compliance.
- Research comprehensive relevant data with source dates, confidence, explicit gaps and low/base/high scenarios. No exhaustive coverage or actual competitor profits claimed.
Record marketing capacity, actual permitted occupancy, seated dinner/dance-floor capacity and weather-backup capacity separately. Add usable event area/acreage, neighboring residences, sound conditions, approved annual events, parking/overflow/shuttle, deal type, asking price/date and real estate inclusion. Seller profitability claims need verification.
## Initial operator observations
- [Deer Park Villa FAQ](https://deerparkvilla.com/faq/) and [packages](https://deerparkvilla.com/packages/): Fairfax/Marin; published capacity 200 indoors and 300 outdoors, layout confirmation required. Preferred vendors are mentioned; unrestricted vendor choice is not established. Midnight permission and total mandatory price unknown.
- [Palm Event Center wedding page](https://www.palmeventcenter.com/get-married/): five-hour reception; indoor/outdoor ceremony options; day-of coordination and food/open-bar service described. Capacity, end time, venue-only availability and full price unknown on this reviewed page. Bundled offering must be normalized before comparison.
- Structured evidence, checked 2026-10-11T03:40:02Z. Marketing capacity is not verified legal occupancy. Neither venue is established as a midnight-compliant match.

# Founder and operator experiences

63 reading records: operator accounts, interviews, advice and separately labeled coach resources. Twenty additional dated publisher interview entries are show-notes-only reviews, not independently reviewed audio. Coverage remains incomplete and biased toward surviving/promotional businesses. Original publication, update and check dates are separate. Missing names/dates remain Unknown.

Read the **Founder experiences** tab for sortable/filterable sources. [Download reading library](founder-experiences.json) · [Readable source notes](founder-experiences.md).

New accounts include Kimberly Keys at White Fallow Estate (2020), Kuyhlia and Vital Hulsbosch at Highpoint Events (2020), Ian Ramirez's current Madera Estates article (2026), and Wenna Hicks's Barn at Pengelly interview/transcript (2026). Source figures are self-reported; none establish Bay Area costs or audited profit.

A cached WeddingPro result returned an older author/version at the same URL. The downloaded current article and live browser agreed on Ian Ramirez, February9,2026; this discrepancy is recorded rather than merging authors/dates.

Remaining gaps: firsthand failure/closure accounts, acquisition operators, California entitlement stories, original audio/video transcripts, historical pricing and independent financial records.


Seven additional original operator accounts cover corporate-career transitions, acquired-property renovations, development timelines, family roles and early operating mistakes. Four have original publication metadata; three remain Unknown. Self-reported opening dates are separate from article dates. No audited startup costs or earnings are supplied.

Nestldown adds a Bay Area firsthand family account: original publication 2020-08-04, revised 2026-08-25. It reports a prolonged approval process and extensive founder labor. Property acquisition in 1991 does not establish wedding opening, permit issuance or operating duration. [Original operator story](https://www.nestldown.com/about-nestldown/).

New readings include Cold Spring Farm’s barn conversion and Eden Gardens’ family succession. A [Paradise Ridge owner-interview case](https://wbj.scholasticahq.com/article/22075-paradise-ridge-winery-can-a-tragedy-strengthen-a-brand), published December 16, 2020, covers wildfire recovery. Its adapted financial tables are not verified competitor accounts. Didi Russell’s anonymous repost is explicitly classified as coach/secondary material; its original owner post is unverified.

# Property and operating feasibility
Early screening questions; no property-specific clearance or commitment.

## Verified starting source
[Solano County special-event facilities](https://www.solanocounty.gov/government/resource-management/planning-services/development-programs/special-event-facilities), checked 2026-10-11T03:33:01Z. Official page describes zoning/size/frequency requirements, permit steps, example fees and involvement of planning, building, environmental health and public works. Applies to unincorporated Solano, not automatically all Bay Area cities/counties. Linked detailed guide not yet reviewed.

## Questions to investigate before commitment
Permitted recurring paid event use at exact parcel/building; transferability of existing permits; capacity, event count, noise, operating hours and alcohol approvals; landlord consent and obligations if approvals fail; assembly occupancy, fire access/exits, accessible facilities, bathrooms, parking/transport, utilities/septic/water, neighbor impacts and weather/emergency backup.

Test venue-only operations: setup/reset, security, cleaning, safety, vendor coordination, rental maintenance, sales/tours and incident response still need assigned responsibility. Customer-hired vendors do not establish owner workload.

Compare all mandatory customer costs with rent, event contribution, operator pay, improvements and cash reserves. Validate actual target-couple interest. Compare land development, existing lawful venue lease and management/revenue-share options after clarifying constraints.

## Hypotheses
Leasing may reduce some development uncertainty, but lease obligations/improvements may still be costly. Creative decor can add labor/storage/reset costs. Land asking price is only part of usable-site cost. Midnight must distinguish music, alcohol, guest departure and cleanup. No cost/profit or permit outcome established.
## Research scope clarification — 2026-10-11T03:38:07Z
- Calculate realistic capital requirements from the evidence; do not impose an upfront budget ceiling or repeat the budget-cap question.
- Compare four routes without selecting one: lease an existing lawful venue; convert leased space; buy land and develop; buy an established venue.
- Desired ability to host 300–400 guests. Whether this is normal or peak capacity remains unknown; no minimum/approved occupancy established.
- Prefer open/separated space to reduce noise issues, but acreage does not establish permitted event use, midnight hours or sound compliance.
- Research comprehensive relevant data with source dates, confidence, explicit gaps and low/base/high scenarios. No exhaustive coverage or actual competitor profits claimed.
Acquisition diligence: business-only leasehold vs business plus real estate; verify financials and owner labor, booking/customer-deposit obligations, deferred maintenance, permit/license/lease transfer, title and contracts. Existing operation does not prove approvals transfer or 400 guests are permitted.
## Midnight research branches confirmed — 2026-10-11T03:40:02Z
Both branches are in scope:
A. Outdoor amplified music and dancing until midnight.
B. Outdoor earlier celebration with indoor late-night music/dancing until midnight.
Also tag fully indoor comparators separately. For each, research lawful hours/noise limits, actual layout/occupancy at 300–400 guests, sound mitigation and staffing, building/weather needs, setup/cleanup, customer experience and all capital/operating costs. Indoor midnight permission is not assumed.
wiki.Four business routes:
# Four-route capital and operations model
Status: framework; sourced dollar estimates not yet collected. Updated UTC: 2026-10-11T03:38:07Z.

| Route | Capital to quantify | Key evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lease lawful venue | Deposit, ramp-up rent, repairs/design, equipment, approvals, professional fees and reserves | Lease terms, permitted use/capacity/hours, quotes |
| Convert leased space | Above plus design, approvals, construction, fire/accessibility/occupancy, utilities, bathrooms, parking | Building/parcel records, approval conditions, scope-specific quotes, lease allocation |
| Buy land and develop | Land/closing, investigations, design/permits, access, utilities/septic, parking, structures, finance carrying costs and reserves | Actual parcels, infrastructure feasibility, approvals, quotes and schedule |
| Buy established venue | Business and/or real estate price, closing/diligence, equipment, repairs, booking liabilities, financing and reserves | Verified financial history, deal structure, permits, contracts/lease and title |

Model 300 and 400 seated guests with dining/dancing and lawful facilities; do not assume land area implies approved capacity. Keep smaller competitors as benchmarks without replacing the desired flexibility.

## Outputs
Total project cost; required cash/equity vs debt; pre-opening carry/time; fixed monthly cost; variable event/headcount cost; contribution; break-even bookings; owner/manager compensation; debt service; booking ramp/seasonality; peak cash deficit and contingency. Capital need is an output, not a predefined ceiling.

Separate operating profit, cash flow and debt repayment. Customer deposits may carry performance/refund liabilities. No confidential competitor profits asserted.

## Every observation
Value/unit, property/route/headcount/date/duration, original source URL/document, quote/publication/check dates, exclusions/taxes, status (verified, asking price, seller claim, assumption, unknown), confidence and sensitivity. Use ranges when one figure is unsupported.

## Acquisition diligence
Business-only/leasehold vs business plus real estate, valuation allocation, actual bookings/revenue/margins, owner labor/add-backs, deposits/unfulfilled events, liabilities/contracts/staff, deferred maintenance, transferable approvals/licenses, lease assignment/title/easements, permitted event count/hours/capacity and reason for sale. Asking price is not valuation.

Initial source: [SBA planning and buying-business guidance](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/plan-your-business/), checked 2026-10-11T03:38:07Z. General guidance, not actual transaction documents or financing quotes.
wiki.Planner workbook:
# What a planner needs from every venue

Original Bay Leaf synthesis • 194 research fields in 18 categories • reviewed October 10, 2026 (Pacific).

Start with suitability, then investigate logistics and complete cost. Every venue gets the same framework; irrelevant fields become **Not applicable** with a reason. Unknown never means allowed, included, free or zero. This is a proposed research standard, not verified answers for all venues.

## The answer format

For each field record: **answer • evidence/status • source URL or written document • date checked • package/date/guest-count assumptions • unresolved question • person responsible • next action/deadline**. Keep quotes and private correspondence in shared private context, not the public website.

Evidence labels: **Authority/document verified; Operator published; Directory reported; Observed on visit; Assumption/calculated; Unknown — inquire; Conflicting; Not applicable; Prohibited/closed**. Written sales answers do not establish legal occupancy. A permission can have conditions; preserve them.

## Research stages

1. Broad inventory: capture leads even when wedding permission is unknown. Do not silently discard unconventional spaces.
2. Uniform inquiry: request terms and itemized prices before tours. Use guest-count scenarios for research without pretending they are booked plans.
3. Joint visit: walk the guest route, supplier route and weather backup with floor plans; check equipment and responsibility gaps.
4. Contract validation: reconcile every promised inclusion and exception with the final terms and relevant approvals.
5. Business review: separately examine repeat use, improvements, operating effort and financial feasibility.

The public comparison should show the useful summary. Expandable details hold the full checklist rather than forcing every question into a very wide table. Filter by status, county, venue type, capacity basis, price basis and restrictions; sort unknowns last.

## Cost per head: compare the same thing

Maintain three distinct measures: **venue-only ÷ guests**, **food/bar package per guest**, and **required event total ÷ guests**. The last is the useful comparison only when all mandatory components are known. It does not include optional photographer, attire or other whole-wedding spending unless explicitly selected.

For a comparable scenario, calculate the applicable venue/space fee + contracted food/bar spend after its minimum + mandatory staffing/rentals + compulsory access, cleaning, transport and permit costs + service charges and tax on their documented bases. Divide by the stated guest count. Count included items once. Keep refundable deposits as cash needed, not an event expense. Avoid adding a package rate to a minimum if the minimum already covers that package.

Record children/vendor-meal treatment and date/season. A “from” price has no known upper bound. If required charges are missing, show a **partial known subtotal**, not an all-in range. Do not manufacture a maximum from an optimistic estimate. Capital required for the business remains a research output, not an imposed budget limit.

## What is especially easy to miss

- A wet-weather room may exist yet be unreserved or too small for dinner plus dancing.
- An item can be available on site without being included; quantities and setup labor matter.
- Vendor lists can be optional, mandatory, or subject to an exception fee.
- A five-hour reception does not identify music cutoff, bar closure, or final departure.
- A high maximum may describe standing use, not the intended seating/dancing layout.
- “Hands-off ownership” still requires named responsibility for safety, guest issues, load-in, cleaning and lockup. Model paid labor and owner hours separately.

## California and Bay Area checks

California ABC states that Type 58 catered alcohol events require event authorization and ordinarily have a 36-event annual limit at a location, with an exception process. This is not a general cap on weddings and does not determine every BYOB arrangement. Treat the alcohol operating route and any exception as a business due-diligence question. [ABC official FAQ](https://www.abc.ca.gov/licensing/license-forms/caterers-permit/).

Accessibility is a continuous experience through arrival, rooms, seating and restrooms. “Historic” or “grandfathered” is not an automatic ADA exemption. [DOJ small-business guidance](https://www.ada.gov/resources/title-iii-primer/).

Do not convert a one-time special-event rental into assumed permission for weekly commercial weddings. Confirm actual jurisdiction, land-use entitlement, permit conditions, occupancy, fire access, noise and food/wastewater requirements for the property. The reviewed Sonoma staff report contains proposed changes, not proof of final adoption; numerical thresholds remain unverified. [Sonoma source](https://sonoma-county.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?GUID=3795E6F1-7701-4414-AB81-C8BB81143BC1&ID=7768001).

## Source review and limitations

- [A Practical Wedding planning workbooks](https://apracticalwedding.com/planner/) — Public resource descriptions reviewed; embedded workbook links not extracted.
- [Here Comes the Guide venue questions and worksheet](https://www.herecomestheguide.com/wedding-ideas/questions-to-ask-your-wedding-venue) — Article and eight-page PDF read; editorial tips are not code requirements.
- [Warrenwood Manor venue shopping workbook](https://warrenwoodmanor.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/Wedding-Venue-Shopping-Guide.pdf) — 15-page PDF read; comparison pages 12–14 visually inspected. Example terms are historical 2021 and Kentucky-specific.
- [Molto Bella venue comparison worksheet](https://www.moltobellaweddings.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/MB_Wedding_Planner_Venue_Comparison.pdf) — One-page PDF read; comparison structure, not California regulations.
- [One Story Weddings venue checklist](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6373bbd7b8f87c3f80597d63/t/692f51c3a7d9fe3ff4687b97/1764708803836/The%2BOne%2BStory%2BWeddings%2BUltimate%2BVenue%2BChecklist.pdf) — Two-page Southern California checklist read; percentage heuristics not adopted.
- [Foothills coordination checklist](https://foothillsconferencecentre.com.au/checklist-for-coordinating-with-wedding-venues/) — Article and two-page PDF read; Australian operational process, not California law.
- [Event Fab producer site inspections](https://eventfab.com/pre-event-site-visits-checklist/) — Production checks reviewed; venue-specific engineering still required.
- [US DOJ accessibility guidance](https://www.ada.gov/resources/title-iii-primer/) — Official guidance reviewed; actual site accessibility requires assessment.
- [California ABC caterer permits](https://www.abc.ca.gov/licensing/license-forms/caterers-permit/) — Official current permit FAQ reviewed; each property and alcohol arrangement must be confirmed.
- [Ready.gov business emergency plans](https://www.ready.gov/business/emergency-plans) — Official public preparedness guidance reviewed.
- [A Savvy Event Napa/Bay Area planning team](https://asavvyevent.com/team/) — Practitioner description supports dedicated onsite production responsibilities, not a standardized workbook.
- [San Francisco entertainment permit guidance](https://www.sf.gov/get-place-entertainment-permit-your-business) — Official search-index text reviewed; direct page verification blocked. No parcel-specific legal conclusion.
- [Sonoma proposed special-event zoning update](https://sonoma-county.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?GUID=3795E6F1-7701-4414-AB81-C8BB81143BC1&ID=7768001) — Staff report reviewed. Agenda Ready status and missing final action mean proposed numbers must not be treated as adopted law.

Five freely accessible PDF workbooks/checklists were downloaded and read for this review. Original source PDFs remain research references and are not republished. Wedding Academy’s paid checklist description was discovered, but its full workbook was not purchased or reviewed. No universal restroom/security ratios, fixed hidden-fee percentage, attendance percentage or venue budget percentage were adopted from these resources. Requirements remain site- and event-specific.

## Venue age and operating history

Record construction year, wedding-operation opening date, current-operator start date and operating duration separately. For multiple structures, identify which building the year describes. Track conversions, rebuilding and interruptions. A historic lodge date does not prove the current reception building was built that year. Exact opening dates allow elapsed years; year-only records produce an approximate duration with an as-of date. Unknown stays Unknown — inquire.

## Value assessment



| Field | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| Parcel/APN, area, zoning, buildings | Confirm the exact asset; a venue address may cover multiple parcels or a leased portion |
| Owner versus operator | Determine what could actually be purchased or leased |
| Last recorded sale and date | Historical transaction, not today's market value; inspect whether it covered these assets |
| Current asking price and scope | Seller expectation; may include land, business, equipment or several properties |
| Assessed land/improvement value and tax year | Tax basis, kept separate from market value |
| Comparable closed sales | Match use, location, condition, acreage/building area and transferable approvals |
| Property estimate low/high | Only when comps or another documented method support the range |
| Business estimate low/high | Requires verified earnings/assets/contracts and valuation assumptions |
| Rent/lease term and assignment | For a tenant operation, land value is not automatically part of the business acquisition |
| Valuation date/method/confidence | Make the estimate reproducible and label evidence gaps |

California tax assessments and current market values can differ because of assessment rules. Do not use the assessed number as a purchase-price estimate. [California BOE explanation](https://www.boe.ca.gov/proptaxes/pdf/lta25023.pdf).

# Venue value assessment

Track **real estate**, **operating business**, and **lease/concession rights** separately. No defensible valuation range has yet been established for the two initial venue records. Unknowns remain explicit; not every venue is for sale.

## Can Zillow help?

Zillow says Zestimates apply to residential properties, excluding commercial property and vacant land. A residential estimate may inform the house component of an estate, but cannot value its wedding operation, event permissions, extra parcels or special-purpose structures. A Zestimate is not an appraisal. [Zillow FAQ](https://www.zillow.com/zestimate/).

## Evidence to collect for each venue

| Field | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| Parcel/APN, area, zoning, buildings | Confirm the exact asset; a venue address may cover multiple parcels or a leased portion |
| Owner versus operator | Determine what could actually be purchased or leased |
| Last recorded sale and date | Historical transaction, not today's market value; inspect whether it covered these assets |
| Current asking price and scope | Seller expectation; may include land, business, equipment or several properties |
| Assessed land/improvement value and tax year | Tax basis, kept separate from market value |
| Comparable closed sales | Match use, location, condition, acreage/building area and transferable approvals |
| Property estimate low/high | Only when comps or another documented method support the range |
| Business estimate low/high | Requires verified earnings/assets/contracts and valuation assumptions |
| Rent/lease term and assignment | For a tenant operation, land value is not automatically part of the business acquisition |
| Valuation date/method/confidence | Make the estimate reproducible and label evidence gaps |

California tax assessments and current market values can differ because of assessment rules. Do not use the assessed number as a purchase-price estimate. [California BOE explanation](https://www.boe.ca.gov/proptaxes/pdf/lta25023.pdf).

## How the research will work

Use assessor/recorder records for parcel and historical facts; [LoopNet's commercial valuation guidance](https://www.loopnet.com/cre-explained/tools/commercial-property-valuation/) and [Crexi commercial listings](https://www.crexi.com/) for relevant sale/lease evidence. Listings are asking prices; sold comps need actual closing dates and asset scope. Restricted or paywalled evidence is recorded as unavailable, not guessed.

Sales comparisons, an income approach and a replacement-cost approach answer different questions. A property's income valuation uses appropriate real-estate operating income and market-supported assumptions, not gross wedding revenue. Unique buildings may have weak comps. The operating business requires separate verification of earnings after normalizing owner labor, market rent, maintenance and one-time costs. A generic earnings multiple is not sufficient evidence for a competitor's valuation.

For an acquisition, model equipment, transferable contracts/approvals, customer deposits and obligations, lease rights, necessary improvements and working capital. Do not add a property value to an earnings-based business value if the same economic benefit is counted twice. Buying an established operation and buying its property are distinct transactions.

Public parks and government sites may offer rentals or concession/lease rights rather than a purchasable venue. Record Not applicable where ownership rules make an acquisition-value field irrelevant, with a reason; replacement cost is a different question.

This is an evidence-collection method. Preliminary ranges, when supported, remain research estimates with dates and assumptions; financing/purchase decisions need property-specific appraisal and business due diligence.


## Why the assessment is not a current venue valuation

Sonoma County explains that assessed values generally begin with a purchase/transfer base year and then receive limited annual adjustments; new improvements can have separate base years. Decline-in-value assessments follow different adjustment rules. Consequently a current roll value does not by itself establish today's market sale price. It also does not price an operating venue business. This is a general county explanation, not a determination of any specific parcel's tax treatment. [County assessment explanation](https://sonomacounty.gov/administrative-support-and-fiscal-services/clerk-recorder-assessor/assessor/real-property/property-value).

The final source check downloaded the county explanation and public parcel-layer metadata. Field aliases were present, but they did not establish a reliable component formula for Value601TotalLI; reconciliation remains Unknown. No additional venue records or research-pass count was claimed for this supporting check.


Final classification check: anonymous Alameda three-ballroom listing broker allocations ($12.3m property/$4.5m business) are preserved as broker_value_claims, with its inconsistent $16.5m combined ask. Independently verified current market-value fields are Unknown. No earnings or appraisal was supplied. This classification correction adds no venue or research pass.

# Angel Island event policy

[California State Parks source](https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=31974), checked 2026-10-11.

Rentals require a special-event permit. Allow at least30days for applications and documents; late filing charges may apply. Outside catering is possible, but vendors pay10% of gross receipts to the park. Alcohol can trigger ABC authorization and insurance. Ferry/charter transport must cover guests, crew and equipment; last sailing and on-island transport require planning. Decorations and amplified sound need approval. Fires/candles and confetti are restricted. Most weddings are incompatible with Immigration Museum rooms. These rules do not establish overnight music rights or a commercial venue lease.

wiki.Public concession case study:
# Public concession case study: Ardenwood

**Historical business evidence; current event concession discontinued.**

The [2024 district RFP](https://www.ebparks.org/sites/default/files/Ardenwood-Cafe-and-Event-ConcessionRFP.pdf) proposed a three-year concession with an optional seven-year extension; no leasehold ownership. Its published historical sales table separates wedding site rent from the broader cafe/event operation:

| Sales year | Total reported sales | Wedding site rent sales |
|---|---:|---:|
|2017|$710,883.07|$115,900.00|
|2018|$837,101.15|$117,475.00|
|2019|$1,002,270.65|$140,800.00|
|2020|$126,673.58|$28,553.74|
|2021|$779,480.07|$124,479.20|
|2022|$675,603.72|$81,000.00|

These are reported sales, **not profit, NOI, valuation, or current forecasts**. No event counts or expense verification establish margin. Do not apply an earnings multiple to gross sales.

The [newer food-only RFP](https://www.ebparks.org/sites/default/files/rfp-ardenwood-cafe-concession.pdf) had a December 1, 2025 deadline, not a current open invitation. In the [January 14, 2026 operations meeting](https://ebparks.new.swagit.com/videos/372115), district staff describe eagle-nesting buffers, cancellations/relocations, and ending the incompatible event concession; the former operator moved to Little Hills. Treat automated meeting transcription as a review aid; verify exact operational status before decisions.

**Bay Leaf lesson (our inference):** habitat restrictions, seasonal event rights and concession tenure belong in the business feasibility model before relying on inexpensive public land. Separate venue-only revenue from catering, alcohol and other sales. A beautiful site and historical midnight access do not establish viable current operating rights.
wiki.Government operating rights:
# Public rental versus operating rights

A one-event rental does not grant commercial control, subletting or ongoing venue operations. Ask for the actual lease, license or concession instrument, permitted uses, term/renewal, fees, restrictions, maintenance, insurance and improvement obligations.

[East Bay Parks 2025 catering RFP](https://www.ebparks.org/sites/default/files/RFP-Caterering-Reservable-Facilities.pdf): historical proposal deadline February10,2025; nonexclusive catering, term ending December31,2026, no leasehold rights. It required an established business and three years of comparable experience; social-event fees were11.5% of pre-tax food/beverage sales. This is catering authorization, not a venue lease. Current procurement/award status must be checked separately.

See the Ardenwood case study for an actual event-concession transition and historical sales evidence. Neither old RFP is presented as an available Bay Leaf opportunity.
wiki.Permission and operating rights:
# Permission to hold a wedding versus operate a venue
Source check: October 11, 2026. This is a research screen, not a property-specific approval. Record the actual jurisdiction, parcel and permit conditions before treating a candidate as feasible.

| Question | Evidence to request |
|---|---|
| Can this exact property host our wedding? | Written confirmation of ceremony/reception use, rooms/grounds, guest layout, date and all deadlines. |
| Can Bay Leaf operate recurring paid weddings here? | Current land-use entitlement, allowed annual event count, operator/ownership conditions, commercial lease or concession rights, and any required amendments. |
| Does outside catering remove venue responsibilities? | Health department classification, food-service infrastructure/plan check, licensed caterer, water/waste/handwashing and permitted alcohol-service plan. |
| Can music run to midnight? | Separate indoor/outdoor amplified-sound limits, permit conditions, contract cutoff and cleanup deadline. An access window is insufficient. |

## Sonoma County: verified current periodic-event pathway
Permit Sonoma's current guidance confirms that the Board adopted the update December 9, 2025, effective June 9, 2026. Its linked consolidated code, displayed as the September 25, 2026 current version, includes the adopted amendments in section 26-22-120. This resolves the earlier draft-versus-adopted verification gap. [Current Permit Sonoma guidance](https://permitsonoma.org/specialeventpermits) · [Current zoning code, section 26-22-120](https://library.municode.com/ca/sonoma_county/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=CH26SOCOZORE_ART22REEDPUASUSST_S26-22-120PESPEV).

The periodic-event pathway allows up to four events on a site in two years. Events at least 30 days apart require separate zoning permits. The attendee cap is 2,500 at any one time, with a specified public-right-of-way/encroachment-permit exception. The code also excludes qualifying events entirely within appropriately permitted buildings and events within the approved use of fairgrounds/outdoor spectator facilities. **Do not apply the occasional-event limit to every approved venue without examining its actual entitlement.** The earlier county staff report separately says winery agricultural promotional standards are unaffected. [County staff report](https://sonoma-county.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?GUID=3795E6F1-7701-4414-AB81-C8BB81143BC1&ID=7768001).

For Bay Leaf, the occasional-event allowance alone cannot support a recurring wedding business. Check the parcel's approved use and commercial operating rights first. The code's agricultural-district restrictions and other applicable approvals remain separate. A public rental or wedding advertisement does not establish permission to lease and operate the property commercially.

The current application guidance requests submissions at least 60 days before an event. Noise follows the county general plan; the 7 AM–11 PM window in the code is one condition of a narrow exclusion, **not a universal licensed venue cutoff**. Music, overnight accommodations, food, tents and associated activities may trigger additional review. The code requires neighborhood notice at least ten days before the event. State and county regional parks use their own agencies' event-permit pathways rather than Permit Sonoma's. Property-specific permission, event frequency and actual indoor/outdoor deadlines remain Unknown until verified.

Evidence checked October 11, 2026 UTC (October 10 Pacific): current agency page and consolidated code reviewed in the live browser; displayed text saved locally. The final signed ordinance document itself was not downloaded, but current agency confirmation and enacted codified text were verified.

## Napa County: temporary-event exemption does not authorize wedding use
The September 23, 2025 staff report on proposed temporary-event changes says weddings and private parties are outside that temporary-event category and fall under other county provisions. Winery marketing is separately defined and subordinate to wine production. This is not permission to turn an agricultural winery into a wedding business. [County report](https://napa.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?FullText=1&GUID=74AAFD7E-5036-4DBF-A49B-C4EDD4C68308&ID=7663685&Options=&Search=).

The newer August 25, 2026 agenda item (26-1526) and current county project page describe an updated proposal, with implementation listed for January 2027 if adopted. The agenda page still displays “Agenda Ready” with no final action. Do not use the older 2025 item as proof of adoption or treat the proposal as current operating permission. [2026 county agenda item](https://napa.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?FullText=1&GUID=35AABC94-AC02-4F2B-8EB9-032AE4766A10&ID=8185096&Options=&Search=) · [County project timeline](https://connect.napacounty.gov/temporary-event-ordinance).

Verification gap: final adoption/current code and each property's grandfathered or approved uses remain unverified. Distinguish unincorporated county land from incorporated cities; keep candidate wedding permission Unknown until property-specific evidence supports it.

## Marin County: identify the actual food-service model
Marin's guidance, updated May 19, 2026, requires a current annual caterer health permit. A host-facility permit applies to a defined model involving direct public sales and venue infrastructure. Its four-hours-in-twelve operational limit is not a blanket four-hour limit on all weddings. The page says that host permit is unnecessary when vendors use none of the venue kitchen, refrigeration, storage, warewashing or other food-service infrastructure. Zoning, fire and other food/alcohol requirements still need their own assessment. [Marin Environmental Health](https://www.marincounty.gov/departments/cda/env-health-svcs/prgm-food/catering-host-facilities).

## Berkeley: current application availability matters
As checked October 11, 2026, Berkeley's official page says new or expanded 2026 special-event applications are no longer accepted; returning/already-queued events are unaffected and 2027 applications are accepted. Its described pathway concerns city street/park events. This does not establish that all private indoor weddings or ordinary facility rentals are unavailable. [City event permits](https://berkeleyca.gov/city-services/event-permits-rentals/special-event-permits).

## Research action
For each serious candidate, request the actual permit and operating contract as well as the customer wedding brochure. Track lawful event frequency, commercial-use rights, caterer infrastructure and sound deadlines independently. Preserve the distinction between rental permission and permission to run Bay Leaf there.

wiki.Solano rural feasibility — 2026 guide:
# Screen rural parcels before comparing acreage prices

The county’s 16-page special-event guide is prepared March 2026, linked by its current planning page. This is unincorporated Solano guidance, not authority for incorporated cities or other counties, and not an issued parcel permit. Current written agency decisions and professional bids remain necessary.

**Midnight feasibility:** page 7 common conditions describe events 10 AM–10 PM, setup/cleanup 8 AM–11 PM and guests departing 10:30 PM except approved lodging. Outdoor amplification guidance is 65 dB at the property line. Standard setbacks 100 ft from property lines/200 ft from adjacent residences are described. Open acreage alone does not grant midnight music; check zoning, issued permit, exceptions and sound design before relying on the business concept.

**Use and time:** agriculture/agritourism zone and small/medium/large classifications determine the permit path; some zones do not permit special events. Guidance estimates administrative review 4–6 weeks and minor/use permits 4–6 months, not guaranteed timelines. Winery marketing events, vacation rentals and B&B lodging do not automatically authorize non-guest weddings. Lodging needs separate approval; guide describes up to 5 rooms/10 attendees where approved.

**Water and wastewater:** water serving 25+ people on 60+ days/year or 15 connections may require a regulated public water system; the guide describes 6–12 months for the process. Food/beverage operation has separate water/health requirements. Small-system threshold wording differs between tables; do not assume 25 people exempt. Septic must match peak design flows. Portable sanitation is a case-specific deferral option, not automatic permission for a 300–400 guest site.

**Access and construction:** building/change-of-occupancy and accessibility review, fire access, accessible parking/routes, year-round parking surface, encroachment and dust/lighting controls can dominate cost. Guide lists tent/canopy fire review above 400 sqft. Its parking ratio is guidance, not proof that any particular guest count is approved. Bella’s draft independently illustrates proposed 20 ft fire driveway, 61 parking spaces, restroom/septic works and road approval; no completed works assumed.

**Fees are only one budget line:** rounded guide planning examples include administrative permit about $1,000, minor permit $2,800, large use permit $6,500; food permits about $1,100–3,100 initial; tent $400; road encroachment $460; septic conventional permit $1,700 / alternative initial $3,000 plus $200 operating fee; small-water annual about $500 plus lab testing. Prior-fiscal-year guide fees change July 1 and are not October 2026 quotes. Fee-table annual renewal charges and five-year permit terms require agency clarification. Guide’s minimum variable septic professional/construction allowance $3,000–10,000 is not an engineered 300–400 guest installed-system budget.

**Model what is absent:** land/lease, due diligence/design, grading/drainage, fire access, water treatment/storage, engineered septic, buildings/tents/ADA, parking/power, insurance, staffing/owner time, marketing, working capital, seasonal demand and contingencies need separate low/base/high quotes. No sum of permit fees is a startup capital estimate, valuation or competitor profit.

Sources: [Current county planning page](https://www.solanocounty.gov/government/resource-management/planning-services/development-programs/special-event-facilities) · [Actual 16-page 2026 guide](https://content.solanocounty.gov/sites/default/files/2026-04/Special_Event_Facility_Guide_APR_2026.pdf) · [Bella draft conditions](https://solano.legistar.com/View.ashx?M=F&ID=11359473&GUID=A7075E28-AE45-4C6E-88D2-A8A1EB1845EB). Pages 5, 7, 14, 15 and draft page 8 visually reviewed from actual downloaded PDFs; current binding code/issued permit verification remains incomplete.

# Bay Leaf overnight research report

[Open the research atlas](https://thenatanzi.github.io/bay-leaf-research/) · [Documented search passes](https://thenatanzi.github.io/bay-leaf-research/discovery-audits.json) · [Coverage audit](https://thenatanzi.github.io/bay-leaf-research/municipality-coverage.json) · [Founder reading library](https://thenatanzi.github.io/bay-leaf-research/founder-experiences.md)

## What is ready

- **1,665 discovery records across all nine Bay Area counties.** These include individual rooms, configurations, packages, closed sites and grouped properties. They are not 1,665 independent available wedding venues.
- **65 venue discovery and fact-check passes**, plus **two founder-library audits**. Each records the missed-venue question, sources, additions or updates, duplicates, exclusions and remaining gaps. The requested ten-pass minimum was exceeded.
- **194 planner workbook criteria in 18 categories**, established before census expansion. The framework covers guest experience, accessibility, weather plans, logistics, complete cost, vendors, contracts and operating feasibility.
- **978 government records** and **1,164 potential/unconventional records**, with overlap. Public rental permission does not establish a commercial lease or concession.
- **887 approximate map points**. A pin is not a surveyed parcel boundary or verified event entrance.
- **77 founder/operator reading sources**, with dates, evidence scope and commercial context. Some are publisher show notes or coach material; they are labeled accordingly. Seventeen lack a known original publication date. Written dates and packet dates remain distinct from publication dates.
- Venue name links, review links, included items, catering/bar/other requirements, Time cut off, cost basis, history and valuation evidence are represented. Price figures distinguish venue-only, food/bar and incomplete package costs; historic rates are not current quotes.

## County record counts

| County | Discovery records |
|---|---:|
| Alameda | 291 |
| Contra Costa | 161 |
| Marin | 143 |
| Napa | 164 |
| San Francisco | 192 |
| San Mateo | 190 |
| Santa Clara | 181 |
| Solano | 180 |
| Sonoma | 163 |

## What remains unknown

**This is an extensive discovery atlas, not a complete or booking-ready inventory.** The coverage audit has 110 municipality/county workstreams; 78 municipal rental workstreams remain labeled Not yet audited. The other 32 have partial reviews, not certified completeness. Private venue coverage also remains incomplete.

Current availability, wedding permission, seated dinner/dance layouts, event/music/alcohol/cleanup deadlines, total quotes and contractual requirements often need direct confirmation. Historical operating and construction dates are separate facts; a building age or copyright year does not establish the first wedding or current operator's tenure.

Only 21 records currently contain a sourced numeric review aggregate. Other Google/Yelp/other links generally provide lookup routes, not verified ratings. Ratings are property/platform aggregates, not room-level quality scores. One advertised paid indoor late-music option is flagged; it is not blanket legal or contractual midnight approval.

Property, land and operating-business value remain separate. Official Sonoma parcel evidence now covers thirteen matched parcels across nine property groups, reflected in 52 shared records. Raw tax assessment fields, historic recorded prices and broker asks are labeled with scope and dates; they are not current market valuations. Some resort transactions span multiple parcels or other assets. Repeated transaction amounts cannot be summed across rooms or parcels. Assessor component definitions and full title/asset scope still need verification. There are no invented competitor profit estimates.

## Next work in order

1. Finish municipality-by-municipality official inventory coverage, including unincorporated areas, and deduplicate to a separate property-level view before comparing market supply.
2. Confirm the shortlist's seated layout, written complete quote, external-vendor rules and separate music/guest/cleanup deadlines. Draft inquiries exist; no inquiries were sent.
3. Resolve exact property ownership/lease, parcel assemblages and permit transferability before using acquisition or operating cost models.

Sonoma County explains that assessed values generally begin with a purchase/transfer base year and then receive limited annual adjustments; new improvements can have separate base years. Decline-in-value assessments follow different adjustment rules. Consequently a current roll value does not by itself establish today's market sale price. It also does not price an operating venue business. This is a general county explanation, not a determination of any specific parcel's tax treatment. [County assessment explanation](https://sonomacounty.gov/administrative-support-and-fiscal-services/clerk-recorder-assessor/assessor/real-property/property-value).

# Bay Leaf: numeric comparison and data audit

Audit of the saved research dataset on October 25, 2026 Pacific. This audits existing evidence; it does not newly verify venue policies, availability or quotes.

## Recommended structure

**A compact numeric comparison, backed by a full venue accordion.** One metric per column, one unit per metric. Keep source wording, dates, conditions, contradictions and all 194 workbook fields in the breakdown.

The first version is implemented in Compare, Government and Potential spaces. Compare defaults to numeric columns and supports numeric minimum/maximum filtering, sorting and reset. The old research/category column views remain available. A dash means Unknown; it never means zero or No. Available platform ratings share one review column; unavailable platforms and search placeholders are omitted there.

## What is already usable as structured numbers

Counts refer to **discovery records**, not independent businesses. Values can be historic, directory-reported, conditional or incomplete; inspect the source and status in the accordion.

| Metric | Records with a structured value | Remaining Unknown |
|---|---:|---:|
| Max published capacity | 968 | 697 |
| Published seated capacity | 437 | 1,228 |
| Published standing capacity | 290 | 1,375 |
| Event fee lower bound | 247 | 1,418 |
| Event fee upper bound | 244 | 1,421 |
| Per-guest package lower bound | 61 | 1,604 |
| Per-guest package upper bound | 59 | 1,606 |
| Sourced numeric review score | 21 | 1,644 |
| Structured numeric construction year | 70 | 1,595 |

There are 1,665 records and 649 distinct parent-property **labels**; those labels have not been verified as unique independent properties. The records include 1,336 spaces, 244 property records, site groups and configurations/packages. A renamed property can create duplicate labels. Combined rooms and their subdivisions can describe the same inventory. A property-level rollup should use a stable property ID, not a name match.

Some usable numbers remain in narrative workbook answers. This table deliberately counts only typed numeric fields. An Unknown numeric cell does **not** mean the source contains no answer. Extracting those additional numbers with source and scope review is the next data-cleaning task.

## How Max capacity works

Max capacity is the largest **structured published figure attached to the same record**: seated, standing, generic, indoor or outdoor. It is not a sum of those alternatives or a legal occupancy determination. The winning figure's basis stays in the accordion.

Example: 150 seated and 225 standing becomes **Max capacity 225**, **Seated capacity 150**. A separate ballroom's count cannot be added. A theater's seated count does not establish tables and a dance floor. Among the 968 records with a max figure, **531 have no separately structured seated figure**.

For selecting an actual wedding, add a distinct **Dinner + dance capacity** metric after the layout is documented. Keep indoor rain-backup capacity separate too. A property rollup should take the highest individually bookable approved layout; it must not add simultaneous rooms unless concurrent use is explicitly supported.

## One combined review column

Show a sortable numeric score, followed by available platform scores, for example **GOOGLE: 3.5 · YELP: 2.7**. This is illustrative; it is not a score assigned to a venue in this dataset.

- Include only a recorded numeric score on a 0–5 scale with a source profile URL. Missing values and unverified search links contribute nothing.
- Deduplicate identical profile URLs if they appear in more than one review slot.
- When all available platform review counts are known and positive, use `sum(rating × count) ÷ sum(count)`.
- If a count is missing, use an equal-platform average and label that method in the breakdown. A single platform retains its own rating; it is not a multi-platform score.
- The displayed rating count is a sum of platform counts, **not deduplicated people**. People can review on multiple platforms. Platform audiences/scales differ, so this is an approximate comparison index, not a statistically calibrated quality measure.
- Preserve each platform's rating, count, URL, check date and scope. A hotel-stay, park or restaurant rating may say little about weddings; a property rating is not room-specific.

Currently Google and Yelp have **zero verified numeric scores** in the saved dataset. The 21 rated records use other recorded platforms. Combining columns does not manufacture Google or Yelp ratings or add new review research. Source checks date from the earlier research run; they are not refreshed by this audit.

## Next fields to quantify, in priority order

| Priority | Comparison field | Type / units | Required qualification kept in accordion |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dinner + dance guests; rain-backup guests | Separate integer counts | Exact room/layout, dance floor, concurrent use, seated versus standing |
| 1 | Venue fee min / max | Two USD/event numbers | Rental hours, season/day, residency/member status, effective date, refundable versus expense |
| 1 | Food min/max; bar min/max | USD/guest, separate components | Minimum guest count, package duration, service/tax bases, actual food included or service-only |
| 1 | Mandatory fixed charges; service %; tax %; minimum spend | Separate USD and percentage fields | Taxable base, mandatory versus optional, no deposits or booking credits counted twice |
| 1 | Scenario event total and cost/guest | Computed low/high USD | Same guest count, date/day, duration and inclusions; show known subtotal when any mandatory component is missing, never label it all-in |
| 1 | Indoor/outdoor music cutoff, guest departure, cleanup | Separate clock times; sortable minutes from event-day midnight | Next-day rollover, weekday/season, amplification, permission versus advertised availability; 8-hour duration is not an 8 PM cutoff |
| 2 | Parking spaces, lodging rooms, beds, toilets, included chairs/tables | Separate integer counts | Exclusive versus shared inventory, item sizes/types, shuttle/valet obligations, rooms versus beds |
| 2 | Event area; property area | Square feet; acres | Usable rentable area versus campus size; parcel scope and indoor/outdoor separation |
| 2 | Required security/coordination staff, labor hours, hourly rates | Counts, hours, USD/hour | Minimum booking/staffing rules, setup/breakdown responsibility, overtime |
| 2 | Hotel/airport travel | Minutes and miles | Named origin/destination, route, mode and time-of-day/date assumptions |
| 3 | Building year; first wedding year; current operator start | Separate years/dates | Different facts; preserve multiple-building scope and conflicts, never derive operation from copyright |
| 3 | Assessed value; asking price; actual closed sale; current appraisal; business value | Separate USD and dates | Full parcel/asset scope, evidence type, earnings basis, land owned versus leased; do not add duplicated real-estate/business earnings |

Prices already in the compact view are **components**, not normalized all-in event totals. A picnic site fee and a resort's base venue fee differ in what they buy; a range alone does not make them equivalent. A package upper bound stays Unknown if only a starting price is published.

## What should remain categorical

Keep county, property/room identity, venue type, vendor policy, wedding permission, accessibility status, restrictions and evidence quality as controlled categories. Binary fields may use Yes / No / Unknown only when the evidence explicitly supports that answer; conditional permission needs its own status. Do not treat category codes as quantities or turn Unknown into No.

Tables/chairs included, outside catering, BYOB, dance floor, amplified music and legal event use are useful explicit flags with conditions in the breakdown. They should not be inferred from marketing photos, a generic rental listing or a venue's silence.

## Evidence model and quality controls

Each normalized fact should carry **value, unit, record/property/room scope, capacity or price basis, source URL, original effective/publication date when known, checked date, evidence status and conflict note**. Maintain original text alongside normalized facts; never replace it.

Recommended field statuses: **Not yet extracted/researched; Searched—no reliable public answer; Requires venue confirmation; Conflicting evidence; Published evidence; Current written confirmation; Not applicable.** A numeric null alone cannot distinguish these. Migrate statuses using actual research logs, not a blanket assumption that every empty field was searched.

The current Fields answered (%) metric counts nonempty answers excluding explicit Unknown/pending text across the 194 criterion slots. It measures recorded-answer coverage, not confidence, completeness of mandatory costs, legal permission or business quality. Not-applicable fields still need a separate documented treatment before using this as a ranking score.

## Implementation now versus next work

**Implemented:** numeric summary, capacity basis preserved, separate seated metric, component price bounds, available-review aggregate, lazy full-record accordion including all workbook fields, numeric range filters, missing-value handling, reset and total-versus-matching record counts. No source facts were discarded and no new venue claims were researched.

**Next:** manually review/extract high-value narrative fields into typed facts; establish stable property and room IDs; normalize comparable event scenarios; verify missing review profiles and dates; introduce field-level research-status filters. Only then add user-adjustable weighted suitability rankings. A numeric-looking score without those foundations would hide uncertainty.

[Machine-readable audit and derived metrics](numeric-audit.json) · [Original research dataset](research.json)


## Approved implementation update — October 25, 2026

The typed evidence model, field-status filters, stable source-group/space IDs, scenario calculator and optional rankings are now implemented. See **Quantification implementation** in this wiki for the delivered features, source checks and unresolved research queues. This original audit above is retained as the baseline, not a statement that all its Next items remain unimplemented.

# Quantification implementation — October 25, 2026 Pacific

The approved audit changes are now implemented in the data model and comparison tools. Existing source facts remain preserved. **Implementation is not the same as finishing source verification:** conditional facts, missing quotes, inaccessible review profiles and unresolved property identities remain explicitly open.

## Use the comparison

1. **Column group:** choose Capacity, Costs, Time cutoffs, Amenities, Travel, History, Valuation or Policies to compare the typed facts. Numeric comparison remains the compact default; the original 194-field research views remain available.
2. **Property groups, research status & review coverage:** switch between all 1,665 records and one representative per source property group; filter a property name/ID; choose any typed fact or one of 194 workbook fields and its research status; find missing review platforms or identity-review cases.
3. **Comparable event scenario & optional assumptions:** set the guest count above, date, rental hours and scope. Blank assumptions stay Unknown. Choose the exact service/tax bases; custom subtotals are available. Use the Scenario columns and each venue's accordion for the cost breakdown.
4. **Optional preference ranking:** choose weights, desired indoor/outdoor music cutoff, vendor preference and optional cost target. No weights or budget target are imposed. Default evidence threshold is 100%. Use Ranking columns to sort the results and inspect the score's evidence coverage.

Settings are temporary planning inputs in this page; they do not change shared venue facts or send inquiries. Reset filters clears filtering; Clear scenario assumptions clears scenario inputs. Ranking weights remain under your control.

## Typed evidence, not numeric-looking guesses

88 typed field definitions now cover capacities, costs, deadlines, inventory, travel, history, valuation and categorical policies. Each extracted fact has a value, status, record scope, extraction method and reference to the original evidence. Unit definitions are centralized; original wording, source URLs/status, source checked date and known effective date are resolved from the referenced record. A missing original publication/effective date stays Unknown. Normalization date does not replace a source's checked date.

Seven statuses distinguish **Not yet extracted/researched; Searched—no reliable public answer; Requires venue confirmation; Conflicting evidence; Published evidence; Current written confirmation; Not applicable.** Empty original slots default to Not yet extracted; they are not automatically marked searched or unavailable. No current written confirmation is invented from an operator brochure or blank contract.

Source-derived values can still be old, conditional, directory-reported or part of a proposal. Provenance displays those limitations. Proposed hourly schedules remain Requires venue confirmation and are excluded from automatic scenario pricing. Conflicting alternatives are held out of the sortable scalar until reviewed.

## Results of the first extraction pass

| Field | Records with an extracted value |
|---|---:|
| Max published capacity | 968 |
| Seated capacity | 438 |
| Explicit dinner + dance count | 12 |
| Event fee minimum | 248 |
| Food-only minimum / guest | 24 |
| Refundable deposit | 157 |
| Indoor music cutoff | 22 |
| Outdoor music cutoff | 34 |
| Cleanup deadline | 22 |
| Security hourly rate | 16 |
| Recorded tables inventory | 27 |

These are counts of records, including repeated rooms/packages, not independent venues or current confirmed bookings. Many numbers are still in conditional narrative. The extraction review queue contains **3254 record/field cases**; they were not converted into unqualified numbers. For example,300seated with unknown dance-floor impact is not a300dinner/dance approval, and a rain tent for 50 does not establish full-event backup.

Explicit dinner/dance examples include county-published dine-and-dance layouts, the Argonaut Maritime Room's 2025 package, and V. Sattui's 170 with-dance versus 200 without-dance layout. These retain date/approval caveats. Picnic table counts are labeled as picnic inventory, not banquet rounds or added occupancy. Bedrooms, beds, tents/cabins and restroom rooms have separate units.

## Stable property and space IDs

All 1,665 records now have stable space/offer IDs and a property-group ID. The registry currently has **649 provisional source groups**. Existing record assignments persist across rebuilds; name edits do not silently recreate IDs. Grouping is not a title/ownership verification or a guarantee of independent inventory.

The property view shows the **highest max-capacity matching record** as representative. Its prices and other metrics belong to that same record; this is not an aggregate of cheapest prices and largest capacities from different rooms. Related rooms/packages remain in the accordion. No capacities, repeated reviews, tax assessments or transaction amounts are summed across alternative configurations.

There are **37 shared-source identity cases** queued for review. Shared government/directory/campus URLs do not prove duplicate properties, so no fuzzy identity merges are made. Actual property-level reconciliation remains research work.

## Cost scenarios

- Event fees, venue-only per-guest rates, food, bar, combined packages, service-only packages and food/bar spend floors are separate. A service-only outside-catering package is not food cost; unresolved allocation remains a gap. A venue-only per-guest charge is multiplied by guest count and compared against its venue minimum, not treated as a food/bar package. Separately identified cleaning charges remain separate components.
- Event fee min/max, hourly rates, included hours and overtime are distinct. Historic proposed rates are never silently treated as current adopted charges.
- Combined food/bar is used once; separate food/bar overrides use a separate-component scenario. A minimum spend contributes only a shortfall. A food/bar floor's service treatment needs a matching selected base.
- Service and tax need explicit charge bases; custom service-charge and taxable subtotals support exceptions. Tax rates are not supplied or guessed by this tool.
- Published additional ceremony charges need a choice to include/exclude them. Security can be calculated from explicit rate, guard count and billable hours, or explicitly treated as included in a fixed-cost assumption. Setup/cleanup staffing conditions remain in the evidence.
- Refundable security/damage deposits are cash requirements, not expenses. Credited booking payments are not charged twice. Conditional deposit tiers are held for review instead of choosing the largest amount.
- Missing mandatory components produce **Known subtotal—incomplete**, with an unresolved-item count and no complete upper total. A full set of user assumptions produces a **Planning estimate**, never a verified all-in venue quote. Date, guest layout, permit and contract applicability still need confirmation.

## Preference rankings

Selected weights use published dinner/dance capacity versus the guest target, indoor/outdoor music versus a chosen deadline, explicit outside-catering policy versus your rule, sourced reviews/5, and complete planning cost versus an optional cost target. Larger-than-needed capacity is not rewarded beyond full credit. Closed/explicitly disallowed sites are not ranked.

Missing criteria reduce ranking evidence coverage; they are not converted into No or zero. Default ranking needs evidence for every selected weight. If you lower the threshold, partial scores remain labeled with their coverage. A score is a preference aid, not proof of lawful wedding use, actual profitability or a completed feasibility study.

## Review verification update

Two additional exact venue/address profiles on **The Knot** were checked through the platform's web reader: [Deer Park Villa](https://www.theknot.com/marketplace/deer-park-villa-fairfax-ca-610322), 4.6 / 40 reviews; [Preservation Park](https://www.theknot.com/marketplace/preservation-park-oakland-ca-286295), 4.7 / 14 reviews. They are added as observations without overwriting the earlier WeddingWire source. Platform populations may overlap; summed counts are not unique people.

Deer Park Villa's operator page displays a Google 4.6 / 225 claim. It remains an **excluded candidate**, not a verified Google aggregate: the linked map yielded no readable rating/profile aggregate. Direct operator download failed certificate validation; direct platform downloads returned 403. No security check was disabled or access block bypassed. Original publication/update dates for those aggregate pages remain Unknown; checked dates are stored separately. No Yelp rating was invented.

## Remaining data work

The feature implementation and first whole-dataset extraction pass are complete. The identity and ambiguous-fact queues, missing review-profile verification, field-specific current quotes, current legal/permit approval and full-source completion remain research tasks. Numeric blanks are visible rather than fabricated. Travel counts and other source-unsupported metrics can legitimately remain Unknown.

[Normalization counts](normalization-audit.json) · [Original and normalized evidence](research.json)


## Documented search outcomes — October 26
A source-reviewed field with no reliable public answer now uses `research_attempts`: field ID, outcome, source URLs, checked date and factual search result. This is distinct from an unsearched blank. Numeric observations take precedence; a negative search never erases a known value. An unresolved capacity conflict remains null/conflicting with its evidence visible. Six new exact Zola profile aggregates preserve counts, platform URL, checked date and mixed couple/professional scope. No new Google/Yelp values were inferred.


## Food assumptions and dated booking holds — October 26

A food-cost override now requires its basis. The user-reported $50/person outside buffet is not prefilled globally. An outside-caterer estimate needs a sourced yes for outside catering; an approved list alone does not establish that the chosen caterer qualifies. A venue-specific quote can instead be entered as an explicit user assumption. Staffing, bar, rentals, taxes and other charges remain separate. Ralston White’s published own licensed/insured-caterer permission is recorded; its transport requirements can add costs.

Sourced date-limited booking holds now make a selected-date scenario incomplete and suppress its preference grade. Villa Chanticleer’s published January1–April9,2027hold is inclusive; absence of a matching hold does not establish availability. Invalid dates do not create complete estimates. Six event hours are not automatically six paid rental hours.

The comparison percentage is labeled Workbook answered: it counts recorded answers to194planner questions, separately from typed facts and research attempts. A low percentage does not mean no research occurred.

# Overnight stays and hidden obligations

The **Overnight stays** column group separates sleeping capacity, included guests/nights, required accommodation units, minimum nights, late-night requirements, and the payer. Each value links to its source and conditions in the full breakdown. Missing values stay Unknown.

**One unit-night is one accommodation unit for one night.** Forty units for two nights is 80 unit-nights, not 80 rooms or guests. A tent, cottage, bedroom and hotel room are different inventory types; beds do not establish legal sleeping occupancy.

## Source-backed examples checked October 26, 2026

| Offer | What is established | What still needs a proposal |
|---|---|---|
| [Dawn Ranch Orchard weekend](https://dawnranch.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Official-2026-Wedding-Packages-Dawn-Ranch.pdf) |40 accommodation units for 2 nights; late-night Lodge option requires 66 units. Lodging is excluded from venue fee. | Dated rates, actual late-night total, taxes/service, contractual payer and unsold-room liability.66is a separately stated Dawn-side requirement; confirm overlap rather than adding 40 plus 66. |
| [Wildhaven two-night weekend buyout](https://www.wildhavensonoma.com/weddings) |40 tents and 7 cabins; full weekend scenario requires 2 nights, 94 unit-nights. Sunday/midweek offers differ. | Price allocation, full obligation and allowed sleeping occupancy;80 beds are not a verified 146-person capacity. |
| [Westerbeke two-night package](https://www.thewesterbekeranch.com/events/details/) | Includes 2 nights for 50 people; service charge 20% applies to stated service/lodging/meal portions. Music and bar end 22:00. | Complete package quote, extra guests, tax basis, room allocation; generic 48/52 overnight maximums need reconciliation. |
| [Straus farmhouse](https://www.straushomeranch.com/weddings/) | Sleeps 8 in 4 bedrooms. | Wedding inclusion/obligation. Separate vacation-rental prices are not automatically wedding prices. |
| [Ralston White](https://ralstonwhiteretreat.org/reservations/overnight-accommodations/) | Operator describes several room/dorm/apartment types. | Current room allocation, total permitted sleepers and current rate documents. Historical 2022 rates are not current quotes. |

## Compare three different money figures

1. **Contractual obligation:** everything someone must commit to, including required lodging, minimum nights, taxes, resort/service/cleaning fees and attrition.
2. **Host net cost:** the host's obligation minus actual, contractually confirmed guest payments that reduce that obligation. Hoping guests will reimburse you does not qualify.
3. **Guest burden:** what guests must pay, required nights and whether attending the wedding requires booking that accommodation.

The shared [coffee worksheet](coffee-worksheet.html) lets you agree on these assumptions. In the atlas scenario, a known mandatory buyout prevents a complete total until it is explicitly accounted for. A fixed-charge lodging assumption must cover all lodging charges and liability. Avoid applying tax/service again to a lodging amount that already includes them; choose a nonoverlapping or custom charge base. No speculative guest reimbursement is deducted.

Other researched obligations include minimum rental/guard hours, extra security, insurance, full-service planner requirements, shuttles, tent/rain contingencies, kitchen limitations, outside-vendor approval, renter cleanup, trash overages and cancellation penalties. See individual source scopes; a policy about a public food sale is not automatically a private-wedding rule.

# Villa Chanticleer: operating an existing public venue

Checked October 26, 2026. This is a historical operating-agreement example, **not an available lease listing, a venue valuation or a profit estimate**. Selected clauses of the city's 52-page agreement and six-page staff report were reviewed; the signature page was visually checked. Later amendments and actual financial results have not been established.

## What the documents establish

| Question | Evidence and limit |
|---|---|
| Who owns the real estate? | The agreement identifies the City of Healdsburg as owner. Operating rights do not transfer land ownership. |
| When did this operator start? | Milestone's effective date is July 1, 2022. Earlier resort and operator history is separate from first wedding operation. |
| How long is the agreement? | Initial five-year term through June 30, 2027; one conditional five-year extension option with notice requirements. An option does not establish that renewal happened. |
| What does the operator give the city? | Section 2 describes consideration through specified free and discounted community rentals. Do not call this a free business: operating obligations remain substantial. |
| What does the operator handle? | Event delivery, staffing, administration, utilities, supplies, security/cleanup and specified upkeep, subject to the agreement's detailed allocation. |
| What does the city maintain? | Specified structural, major equipment and building components. Funding remains subject to public budgeting; responsibilities are not interchangeable with an ordinary private lease. |
| What financial evidence is missing? | The agreement requires an annual revenue/expense report. Actual reports, normalized earnings, assets/liabilities and transferable business value have not been verified here. |

[City operational transition](https://healdsburg.gov/1032/2022-Villa-Chanticleer-Operational-Trans) · [2022 agreement, especially §§2, 5–7, 11–13 and Exhibit 4](https://healdsburg.gov/DocumentCenter/View/15329/Villa-Chanticleer-Management-Agreement-with-Milestone-2022) · [June 21, 2022 staff report](https://healdsburg.gov/DocumentCenter/View/15330/Milestone-Events-Group-Management-Agreement-City-Council-Staff-Report).

## A useful contradiction

The staff report describes **six** waived Legion events annually; the signed agreement's §7.4(c) states **three**. Preserve both source versions and check amendments before relying on an obligation. Do not project revenue from a staff summary alone. The staff report's historical city maintenance budget and estimated community-benefit value are neither the operator's total expenses nor its profit.

## A current operating constraint

The city reports a **January 1–April 9, 2027 booking hold** for proposed kitchen, bar and entrance-accessibility work. Its stated **$1.5 million state grant** is project funding, not the property's market value or the operator's purchase price. Completion and revised booking dates need confirmation. [City modernization project](https://www.cityofhealdsburg.org/1200/Villa-Chanticleer-Modernization-Project).

The operator advertises a wedding offer for up to **250 guests**, base event time **4–10 PM**, and an extension toward midnight at **$500/hour**. This does not establish midnight music or a complete event price. The city's larger generic occupancy figures apply to different configurations. [Operator wedding offer](https://milestoneeventsgroup.com/venue/villa-chanticleer/).

## What this changes in Bay Leaf's feasibility work

- Add public operating agreements and concessions as a specific version of the **lease an established lawful venue** route. A one-day public room rental is a different transaction.
- Price replacement management labor, utilities, maintenance, community discounts and downtime. Land acquisition can be avoided while meaningful operating obligations remain.
- Check permitted use, assignment, renewal, capital-work allocation and inherited bookings before modeling an acquisition or operating-rights transfer.
- Keep property value, business value, capital grants, gross revenue and profit in separate fields. The evidence here supports no current appraisal or earnings valuation.

The other routes remain: convert a leased space, buy/develop land, or acquire an established venue/business. None inherits this agreement's economics automatically.

- **Develop land:** TerrAdorna describes code changes between initial inquiry and building; Emerson Fields describes infrastructure, owner labor and cash runway. Obtain current approvals and budget contingency before relying on cheap land.
- **Acquire an operating venue:** Sarah Chung’s Matthews House account describes utilities, landscaping, repairs and a delayed improvement permit. Purchase price alone does not establish the money required to operate.
- **Convert existing property:** Maple Ridge and Echo Valley show retreat/farm buildings evolving into wedding and lodging operations. Guest movement, restrooms, climate control, staffing and classification require their own review.
- **Lease a lawful venue:** These interviews do not establish a California lease/concession opportunity. Existing Bay Leaf public operating-agreement evidence remains separate from ordinary event rentals.

For each route, explicitly assign someone and a cost for tours/sales, contracts, vendor checks, event supervision, equipment setup, toilets/waste, landscaping, cleaning, maintenance and emergencies. Outsourcing changes the labor line rather than making the task disappear. Included/optional/mandatory lodging needs a separate contract and payer analysis. None of these interviews supplies a verified Bay Leaf budget or competitor profit.
